examples.en: The tree roots stretch deep into the ground.
A tree root was sticking out of the road and I almost tripped.
Many trees were pulled out by the roots in the typhoon.
Please give plenty of water around the tree's roots.

examples.ko: 이 나무뿌리는 말려서 차로 끓여 마셔요.
examples.en: You dry this tree root and boil it as tea.
The paving stones are lifted up because of the tree roots.

explain: 그냥 '뿌리'라고 해도 돼요. 나무인 것을 분명히 하고 싶을 때 '나무뿌리'라고 말해요. '뿌리'는 '문제의 뿌리'처럼 근본을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: You can simply say '뿌리'. People say '나무뿌리' when they want to make clear it is a tree's root. '뿌리' is also used figuratively for the origin of something, as in '문제의 뿌리'.

examples.ko: 이 오래된 나무줄기가 굵고 튼튼해 보여요.
examples.en: The trunk of this old tree looks thick and strong.
The monkey grabbed the trunk and climbed up.
They put a name tag on the tree trunk.
Insects are living inside the tree trunk.
In winter, people wrap straw around the tree trunks.
When it rained, the tree trunk got wet and dark.

explain: 그냥 '줄기'라고도 많이 말해요. '줄기'는 나무뿐 아니라 풀, 꽃, 채소에도 쓰지만, '나무줄기'는 나무에만 써요. 나무의 몸통 부분을 가리킬 때 자연스러워요.
explain_en: People often just say '줄기'. '줄기' is also used for grass, flowers and vegetables, but '나무줄기' is only for trees. It is natural when you mean the main body of a tree.

en: piece of wood; block of wood; chunk of wood

examples.en: The child is building a house with wooden blocks.
I gathered pieces of wood to make a fire.
A small piece of wood is rolling around on the floor.
I used a block of wood instead of a chair.
He carved a piece of wood with a knife and made a doll.
I put a piece of wood under the desk leg.

explain: '토막'은 잘라 낸 한 조각을 말해서, 나무토막은 잘려 있는 나무 조각이에요. 불 피울 때 쓰는 나무는 '장작'이라고 해요. 집 짓기 놀이를 하는 장난감 블록도 나무토막이라고 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: '토막' is a cut-off piece, so a 나무토막 is a piece of wood that has been cut. Wood used for a fire is called '장작'. Wooden toy blocks for building can also be called 나무토막.

examples.en: My mother made a refreshing nabak-kimchi.

examples.ko: 나박김치 국물이 시원해서 자꾸 먹게 돼요.
examples.en: The nabak-kimchi broth is so refreshing that I keep eating it.

examples.ko: 고기를 먹을 때 나박김치를 같이 먹어요.
examples.en: I eat nabak-kimchi together when I have meat.
Radish and cabbage go into nabak-kimchi.
The nabak-kimchi at this place is really delicious.
When the nabak-kimchi ripens, it gets even more refreshing.

explain: 국물이 많은 물김치라서 배추김치와 달리 국물을 같이 떠먹어요. 맵지 않고 시원한 맛이라 기름진 음식이나 떡과 잘 어울려요. 김치지만 반찬이면서 국처럼 먹는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is a watery kimchi, so unlike napa cabbage kimchi you also scoop up and drink the broth. It is mild and refreshing, so it goes well with oily food or rice cakes. It is a side dish but is eaten a bit like a soup.

examples.en: Anglers are gathered by the lake.
My father is a well-known angler.
The angler caught a big fish.

examples.ko: 새벽부터 낚시꾼 몇 명이 강가에 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: A few anglers have been sitting by the river since dawn.
It is a popular spot for anglers.

examples.ko: 저 낚시꾼은 하루 종일 한 마리도 못 잡았어요.
examples.en: That angler didn't catch a single fish all day.

explain: '-꾼'은 어떤 일을 자주 하거나 잘하는 사람에게 붙어요. 낚시를 즐기는 사람을 말할 때 '낚시꾼'이라고 해요. 가볍게 한 번 해 본 사람은 '낚시하는 사람'이라고 말하는 편이 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '-꾼' is added to someone who does something often or is good at it. '낚시꾼' is someone who really enjoys fishing. For someone who just tried it once, '낚시하는 사람' sounds more natural.

examples.en: My younger brother isn't really focused on fishing and just talks.
I go fishing by the river every weekend.

examples.ko: 낚시질에 빠진 뒤로 집에 잘 안 있어요.
examples.en: Ever since he got hooked on fishing, he's hardly ever at home.
Fishing is prohibited at this lake.
I bought bait before going fishing.

examples.ko: 처음 한 낚시질이라 아무것도 못 잡았어요.
examples.en: It was my first time fishing, so I caught nothing.

explain: 일상에서는 '낚시'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '낚시질'은 낚시하는 일 자체를 말할 때 쓰고, '-질'이 붙어 조금 투박하게 들릴 수 있어요. 보통은 '낚시를 하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: In daily life '낚시' sounds much more natural. '낚시질' refers to the act of fishing itself, and with '-질' it can sound a bit blunt. Usually people say '낚시를 하다'.

examples.en: The man cast his fishing rod far out.
The tip of the fishing rod bent a lot.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 낚싯대만 들고 있는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people hold only a fishing rod all day long.
My fishing rod broke, so I bought a new one.
I bought my child a small fishing rod.
I loaded two fishing rods into the car.

explain: '낚싯대를 던지다', '낚싯대를 드리우다'처럼 말해요. 낚시 도구에는 낚싯줄, 낚싯바늘, 찌도 있어서 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: You say '낚싯대를 던지다' or '낚싯대를 드리우다'. Other fishing gear includes the line (낚싯줄), the hook (낚싯바늘) and the float (찌), which are good to learn together.

examples.en: A big fish got caught on the fishhook.
First, you put the bait on the fishhook.
This fishhook is very sharp, so be careful.
I accidentally pricked my finger on the fishhook.
The tip of the hook was bent, so I replaced it with a new one.

examples.ko: 낚시 가게에서 낚싯바늘을 한 봉지 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pack of fishhooks at the fishing shop.

explain: 물고기가 '낚싯바늘에 걸리다'라고 말하고, 사람이 찔릴 때는 '찔리다'를 써요. '바늘'만 쓰면 바느질 바늘로 들리니까 낚시 얘기에서는 '낚싯바늘'이라고 해요. 낚싯대, 낚싯줄과 같이 낚시 도구로 묶어서 외워요.
explain_en: A fish 'gets caught' on it (낚싯바늘에 걸리다), and a person gets pricked (찔리다). '바늘' alone sounds like a sewing needle, so use '낚싯바늘' when talking about fishing. Learn it together with 낚싯대 and 낚싯줄.

examples.en: We went out to sea on a fishing boat at dawn.
A fishing boat is coming into the harbor.

examples.ko: 낚싯배는 보통 열 명쯤 탈 수 있어요.
examples.en: A fishing boat can usually carry about ten people.
I caught a big sea bream on the fishing boat.
The waves were high, so the fishing boat rocked a lot.
I booked a fishing boat for this weekend.

explain: 낚시하는 사람을 태워 주는 배를 말할 때 많이 써요. 고기 잡는 일을 하는 배는 '고깃배'나 '어선'이라고 해요. 배를 세는 말은 '척'이에요.
explain_en: It is often used for a boat that takes people out to fish. A boat used for the fishing trade is a '고깃배' or '어선'. The counter for boats is '척'.

examples.en: You must cook raw meat before eating it.
I wonder if it's okay to give raw meat to a cat.
Wash your hands right away after touching raw meat.
I use separate cutting boards for raw meat and vegetables.
The fridge smells like raw meat.
I ate raw meat by mistake and got a stomachache.

explain: '날-'은 익히지 않은 것에 붙어요. 날달걀, 날것처럼 짝으로 같이 알아 두세요. 불에 익힌 고기는 '익힌 고기'라고 하고, 날고기는 '생고기'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '날-' attaches to things that are not cooked, as in 날달걀 and 날것. Cooked meat is '익힌 고기', and raw meat is also called '생고기'.

examples.en: I mixed a raw egg into my rice and ate it.

examples.ko: 날달걀을 먹으면 배탈이 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: Eating raw eggs can give you a stomachache.
Beat one raw egg into the bowl.
There are three raw eggs in the fridge.

examples.ko: 날달걀과 삶은 달걀은 돌려 보면 구별돼요.
examples.en: You can tell a raw egg from a boiled one by spinning it.
Please crack raw eggs carefully so the shell doesn't fall in.

explain: 익히지 않은 달걀은 '날달걀'이나 '생달걀'이라고 하는데, 일상에서는 '날달걀'이 더 자주 들려요. 반대말은 '삶은 달걀', '구운 달걀'처럼 조리 방법으로 말해요. '날계란'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: An uncooked egg is called '날달걀' or '생달걀', and '날달걀' is heard more in daily talk. The opposites are described by cooking method, like '삶은 달걀' (boiled egg) and '구운 달걀' (baked egg). People also say '날계란'.

examples.en: I was scared because I was left alone at home.
A lot of food has been left over.
The person who is left last turns off the lights.
All that was left to him was an old watch.
All my friends left and only I was left behind.
A note had been left on the desk.

explain: '남다'는 저절로 남는 것이고, '남기다'는 누가 일부러 남기는 것이에요. '남겨지다'는 남기다의 피동으로, 내가 원하지 않았는데 남은 느낌이 강해요. 특히 사람이 혼자 두고 간 곳에 '남겨지다'라고 하면 쓸쓸한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: '남다' is something that remains by itself, and '남기다' is someone deliberately leaving it. '남겨지다' is the passive of 남기다 and feels like being left against your will. Used for a person left alone, it sounds lonely.

examples.en: Many people hope for Korean reunification.

examples.ko: 남북통일이 되면 기차로 유럽까지 갈 수 있을까요?
examples.en: If the Koreas were reunified, could we travel to Europe by train?
We learned about Korean reunification in class today.
Our class debated the topic of Korean reunification.

examples.ko: 할머니는 남북통일을 꼭 보고 싶다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother said she really wants to see reunification.
We talked about how much reunification would cost.

explain: 뉴스나 수업에서는 '통일'이라고만 줄여 말할 때도 많아요. '통일을 하다'보다는 '통일이 되다', '통일을 이루다'처럼 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '평화통일'도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In the news and in class it is often shortened to just '통일'. People usually say '통일이 되다' or '통일을 이루다' rather than '통일을 하다'. A related term you will often see is '평화통일'.

examples.en: The men's clothing section is on the third floor.
This brand also makes men's clothing.
I picked out a suit in the men's section.
I bought men's clothes as a gift for my father.
Men's clothing seems to have fewer types than women's clothing.
These days men's clothes come in many colors too.

explain: 반대말은 '여성복'이고, 아이 옷은 '아동복'이라고 해요. 백화점이나 옷 가게 안내판에서 자주 볼 수 있어요. 말로 할 때는 '남자 옷'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '여성복', and children's clothes are '아동복'. You often see it on department store and shop signs. In speech, people also say '남자 옷'.

examples.en: Because it's a south-facing house, sunlight comes in well even in winter.
I went to a real estate office to find a south-facing house.
South-facing houses are a bit more expensive than others.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 남향집이 아니라서 낮에도 어두워요.
examples.en: Our house doesn't face south, so it's dark even in the daytime.

examples.ko: 저는 햇빛 잘 드는 남향집에서 살고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to live in a sunny south-facing house.
I'm looking for a south-facing house to move into.

explain: 집이 바라보는 방향은 '남향', '동향', '서향', '북향'이라고 해요. 한국에서는 집을 구할 때 햇빛이 잘 드는지가 중요해서 '남향'이라는 말이 자주 나와요. 아파트는 '남향집'보다 그냥 '남향'이라고 말하는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: The direction a house faces is called 남향, 동향, 서향 or 북향. When looking for a home in Korea, sunlight matters, so '남향' comes up often. For apartments, people often just say '남향' rather than '남향집'.

examples.en: I stopped walking in front of the cliff.
The side of the road was a steep drop, so I was scared.
I had a dream of falling off a cliff.
Please don't go toward the cliff edge.
There are many steep drops on the mountain trail, so be careful.
You can see the sea below the cliff.

explain: '절벽'은 높고 가파른 바위 벽 자체를 말하고, '낭떠러지'는 그 끝에서 아래로 떨어지는 위험한 곳을 말할 때 자연스러워요. '낭떠러지에서 떨어지다', '낭떠러지 끝에 서다'처럼 써요. 위험한 상황을 비유할 때도 나와요.
explain_en: '절벽' is the steep rock wall itself, while '낭떠러지' feels natural when you mean the dangerous drop at the edge. You say '낭떠러지에서 떨어지다' or '낭떠러지 끝에 서다'. It can also be used figuratively for a dangerous situation.

examples.en: This museum is free for citizens.
There are separate lines for citizens and foreigners.
The number of domestic tourists has also grown a lot.

examples.ko: 이 행사는 내국인만 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only citizens can apply for this event.
The price is different for foreigners and citizens.
I used the citizens-only counter at the airport.

explain: 반대말은 '외국인'이에요. 안내문, 뉴스, 관광지 요금표에서 자주 나오고 일상 대화에서는 '한국 사람'이라고 많이 말해요. 공항 창구나 박물관 입장료에서 '내국인/외국인'으로 나누어요.
explain_en: The opposite is '외국인'. It appears on notices, in the news and on tourist-site fee tables, while in daily talk people usually say '한국 사람'. Airport counters and museum fees are split into 내국인 and 외국인.

examples.en: You can see the sea below from my room's window.
From the top of the hill, you can see the whole village below at a glance.
You can see the park below from our balcony.
The whole city was visible below from the observation deck.
We went to a cafe with a view down over the river.

examples.ko: 높은 데 올라가니 차들이 작게 내려다보여요.
examples.en: When you climb up high, the cars look small below.

explain: '내려다보다'는 내가 일부러 보는 것이고, '내려다보이다'는 높은 곳에서 아래 풍경이 저절로 눈에 들어오는 거예요. 보이는 것에 '이/가'를 붙여요. 반대말은 '올려다보이다'예요.
explain_en: '내려다보다' is looking down on purpose, while '내려다보이다' means the view below simply comes into sight from a high place. The thing seen takes '이/가'. The opposite is '올려다보이다'.

examples.en: From the upper floor they sent down a basket tied to a rope.
I sent the child downstairs first.
We sent a rope down and pulled the things up.
I'll send the heavy luggage down first.
They are letting the passengers off one by one.
My parents sent me down to the countryside during vacation.

explain: 반대말은 '올려보내다'예요. 서울에서 지방으로 갈 때 '내려가다'라고 하듯이, 사람을 지방으로 보낼 때도 '내려보내다'라고 해요. 앞에 보내는 대상을 '을/를'로 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '올려보내다'. Just as going from Seoul to the provinces is '내려가다', sending someone there can be '내려보내다'. The thing or person sent takes '을/를'.

examples.en: My mother served tea to the guest.
Grandmother brought out some delicious side dishes.
He took money out of his pocket and put it out.
He did not give up his seat.
They put goods out in front of the shop and sell them.
Everyone put forward honest opinions at the meeting.

explain: 일상에서는 줄여서 '내놓다'(내놓아요)를 훨씬 자주 말해요. 음식이나 돈을 꺼내 보이거나, 자리나 생각을 양보하거나 말할 때 써요. 새 상품을 시장에 내놓을 때도 '내놓다'를 써요.
explain_en: In daily speech people use the shortened '내놓다' (내놓아요) much more often. It is used for bringing out food or money, giving up a seat, or putting forward an opinion. It is also used for putting a new product on the market.

examples.en: In summer, cold soup brings back your appetite.
I floated ice in the cold soup and ate it.
I put julienned cucumber into the cold soup.
The cold soup was so refreshing that I finished my rice quickly.
Please give me one more bowl of cold soup.
My mother made me cold soup.

explain: 차갑게 먹는 국이라서 따뜻한 국과 달라요. 오이냉국, 미역냉국처럼 앞에 재료 이름을 붙여서 많이 말해요. 여름 식탁에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a soup eaten cold, unlike a hot soup. People often put the main ingredient before it, as in 오이냉국 (cucumber) and 미역냉국 (seaweed). You see it often on summer tables.

examples.en: Please put the leftover side dishes in the fridge compartment.
The fridge compartment door doesn't close properly.
I slowly thaw the meat from the freezer in the fridge compartment.
I lowered the temperature of the fridge compartment a little.

examples.ko: 우유는 냉장실 맨 위 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The milk is on the top shelf of the fridge compartment.

examples.ko: 냉장실이 꽉 차서 더 못 넣어요.
examples.en: The fridge compartment is full, so I can't put in any more.

explain: 냉장고 안에서 얼리지 않고 차갑게 보관하는 칸을 말하고, 반대는 얼리는 '냉동실'이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '냉장고'라고 하는 경우가 많아요. 칸을 나눠서 말할 때 냉장실과 냉동실이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the part of the refrigerator that keeps food cold without freezing, and the opposite is the freezer, '냉동실'. In daily speech people often just say '냉장고'. You use 냉장실 and 냉동실 when separating the two compartments.

examples.en: Four or five friends came over to hang out.
I bought four or five apples at the market.
We meet around four or five o'clock.
The kids look to be about four or five years old.

examples.ko: 집이 멀어서 버스를 네다섯 번 갈아탔어요.
examples.en: My home is far, so I changed buses four or five times.

examples.ko: 저는 한 달에 책을 네다섯 권 읽어요.
examples.en: I read about four or five books a month.

explain: 정확한 숫자를 모를 때 어림잡아 말해요. 뒤에 '명, 개, 시, 살, 권'처럼 세는 말이 와요. '네댓'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰고 말할 때는 이쪽도 자주 들려요.
explain_en: You use it to give an approximate number when you don't know the exact one. A counter such as 명, 개, 시, 살 or 권 follows it. '네댓' has the same meaning and is also heard often in speech.

examples.en: We held an impromptu singing contest at the party.
I took part in our village's singing contest.
The first prize at the singing contest is a refrigerator.
Grandmother won a prize at the singing contest.
We decided to have a singing contest at the company dinner.
A singing contest is being broadcast this evening.

explain: 동네 잔치나 모임, 방송에서 여러 사람이 차례로 나와 노래를 부르는 대회예요. '노래자랑에 나가다', '노래자랑을 열다'처럼 말해요. 전문 가수를 뽑는 오디션보다 가볍고 즐거운 분위기예요.
explain_en: It is an event, at a village festival, gathering or on TV, where people take turns singing. You say '노래자랑에 나가다' or '노래자랑을 열다'. It has a lighter, more fun mood than an audition to choose professional singers.

examples.ko: 구청에서 노점 단속을 강화하자 상인들이 반발했어요.
examples.en: When the district office stepped up its crackdown on street stalls, the vendors pushed back.
I bought hotteok from a street stall on my way home from work.
Street stalls line up in front of the market.
The woman at the street stall gave me extra tangerines.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에는 노점이 문을 안 열어요.
examples.en: On rainy days the street stalls don't open.
Grandmother sells wild greens at a street stall.

explain: 길가에 건물 없이 물건을 놓고 파는 가게예요. 장사하는 사람은 '노점상'이라고 하고, 천막을 치고 음식과 술을 파는 곳은 '포장마차'라고 해요. 뉴스에서는 단속이나 상권 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a stall selling goods at the roadside without a building. The seller is a '노점상', and a tent stall selling food and drinks is a '포장마차'. In the news it often appears in stories about crackdowns or shopping districts.

examples.en: I couldn't hide my surprise.
Surprise and joy mixed together at the sudden news.

examples.ko: 아이들은 놀람 반 기쁨 반으로 선물을 열었어요.
examples.en: The children opened the gift half in surprise and half in joy.

examples.ko: 놀람 때문에 한동안 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: I couldn't speak for a while because of the shock.

examples.ko: 그 소식은 우리에게 큰 놀람을 주었어요.
examples.en: That news gave us a big surprise.
A look of surprise filled his face.

explain: 말할 때는 보통 '놀랐어요'처럼 동사를 쓰고, 명사 '놀람'은 글이나 감정을 설명할 때 나와요. '놀라움'은 감탄이나 대단하다는 느낌이 있고, '놀람'은 깜짝 놀라는 느낌에 더 가까워요. '놀람을 금치 못하다'는 뉴스에서 쓰는 표현이에요.
explain_en: In speech people usually use the verb, as in '놀랐어요', and the noun '놀람' appears in writing or when describing feelings. '놀라움' carries a sense of wonder or admiration, while '놀람' is closer to being startled. '놀람을 금치 못하다' is an expression used in the news.

examples.ko: 아빠! 이번 주말에 놀이동산에 놀러 가요.
examples.en: Dad! Let's go to the amusement park this weekend.

examples.ko: 놀이동산은 사람이 너무 많아서 줄이 길어요.
examples.en: The amusement park is so crowded that the lines are long.
Yesterday I rode a roller coaster at the amusement park.
The kids keep begging to go to the amusement park.
I bought an all-day pass for the amusement park with my friend.
I watched a parade inside the amusement park.

explain: 롤러코스터, 회전목마 같은 놀이기구가 있는 곳이에요. '놀이공원'이라고도 말해서 둘 다 알아 두면 좋아요. '놀이동산에 가다', '놀이동산에서 놀다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a place with rides such as roller coasters and carousels. People also say '놀이공원', so it is good to know both. You say '놀이동산에 가다' or '놀이동산에서 놀다'.

examples.ko: 유아 전용 놀이방이 있는 식당이라 아기 손님이 많이 와요.
examples.en: It's a restaurant with a play room for little kids, so many baby customers come.
I leave my child at the daycare and go to work.
At the daycare, he plays with blocks with his friends.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 놀이방은 오후 일곱 시까지 열어요.
examples.en: The daycare in our neighborhood is open until seven in the evening.

examples.ko: 놀이방 선생님이 아이를 잘 돌봐 주세요.
examples.en: The daycare teacher takes good care of the child.

examples.ko: 거실 한쪽에 아이 놀이방을 따로 만들었어요.
examples.en: We made a separate play room for the child in one corner of the living room.

explain: 아이를 돌봐 주는 시설을 말하기도 하고, 식당이나 집 안에 아이가 놀 수 있게 만든 공간을 말하기도 해요. 시설을 말할 때는 요즘 보통 '어린이집'이라고 불러요. 뜻이 두 가지라서 문장에서 시설인지 공간인지 구분해서 읽어요.
explain_en: It can mean a facility that looks after children, or a space in a restaurant or home made for kids to play. For the facility, people now usually call it '어린이집'. Since it has two meanings, check from the sentence whether it is a facility or a space.

examples.en: I bought the baby a safe toy.
Even a single box is a good plaything for a child.
Toys are scattered all over the floor.
The puppy came carrying its toy in its mouth.
Now put the toys away and go to sleep.
The kids share the toys with each other.

explain: '장난감'과 비슷하지만 '놀잇감'은 가게에서 산 물건이 아니어도 놀이에 쓰이는 것은 다 가리킬 수 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '장난감'이 더 흔하고, '놀잇감'은 아이 교육이나 육아 이야기에서 자주 들려요. 아이뿐 아니라 강아지에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is similar to '장난감', but 놀잇감 can refer to anything used for play, even if it wasn't bought in a store. In daily conversation '장난감' is more common, and 놀잇감 is heard more in talk about education and child-rearing. It can be used for pets too, not just children.

examples.en: I meet my friends at the basketball court on weekends.
A new basketball court opened next to the school.
It rained, so the basketball court floor is slippery.

examples.ko: 농구장은 밤 열 시에 문을 닫아요.
examples.en: The basketball court closes at ten at night.
There were many people at the basketball court, so I waited.
We played basketball at an outdoor court.

explain: 농구를 하는 장소를 말하고, 축구장, 야구장처럼 '-장'이 붙은 말과 같은 짝이에요. 농구 경기를 크게 하는 곳은 '농구 경기장'이라고도 해요. 길가에 있는 작은 곳은 보통 '농구장'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is a place for playing basketball, in the same group as 축구장 and 야구장. A large venue for games can also be called '농구 경기장'. A small court out in the neighborhood is usually just called '농구장'.

examples.en: I bought new basketball shoes last week.

examples.ko: 이 농구화는 발목을 잘 잡아 줘요.
examples.en: These basketball shoes support your ankles well.
My basketball shoe lace came undone, so I tied it again.
You have to wear basketball shoes in the gym.

examples.ko: 형은 농구화를 아껴서 늘 깨끗이 닦아요.
examples.en: My older brother takes care of his basketball shoes and always cleans them.

examples.ko: 농구화가 커서 양말을 두 켤레 신어요.
examples.en: The basketball shoes are big, so I wear two pairs of socks.

explain: 운동할 때 신는 신발 이름에는 축구화, 러닝화, 등산화처럼 종목 이름을 붙여요. 신발을 세는 말은 '켤레'예요. 신발은 '신다'를 써서 '농구화를 신다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Shoes for sports are named by adding the sport, as in 축구화, 러닝화 and 등산화. The counter for shoes is '켤레'. You wear shoes with '신다', so it is '농구화를 신다'.

examples.en: My parents still farm in the countryside.
Grandfather sent me rice that he grew himself.

examples.ko: 사막화로 농사짓던 땅을 잃은 사람들이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More and more people are losing the land they used to farm because of desertification.
It's hard to farm because there is no rain.
I had no land to farm, so I came to the city.

examples.ko: 우리 이웃은 산 밑에서 농사지으며 살아요.
examples.en: Our neighbor lives farming at the foot of the mountain.

explain: '짓다'는 ㅅ 불규칙이라서 '지어요', '지은', '지을'처럼 ㅅ이 빠져요. '농사를 짓다'처럼 띄어 써도 되고, 한 단어로 붙여서 '농사짓다'라고 써도 돼요. 쌀이나 고추처럼 작물을 쓸 때는 '고추 농사를 짓다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '짓다' is an ㅅ-irregular verb, so the ㅅ drops in forms like '지어요', '지은' and '지을'. You can write it spaced as '농사를 짓다' or as one word, '농사짓다'. With a crop such as rice or peppers, '고추 농사를 짓다' sounds natural.

examples.en: We did the high jump at the school sports day.
A high jump athlete really flies high.
His body caught the high jump bar.
I find the long jump easier than the high jump.
This year's high jump record is better than last year's.
I watched the high jump final on TV.

explain: 육상 경기 종목 이름이에요. 비슷한 종목으로 '멀리뛰기', 장대를 쓰는 '장대높이뛰기'가 있어요. 운동은 '높이뛰기를 하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is the name of a track and field event. Similar events are '멀리뛰기' (long jump) and '장대높이뛰기' (pole vault). You say '높이뛰기를 하다' for doing it.

examples.en: This morning I boiled and ate some toasty nurungji.
Nurungji has stuck to the bottom of the rice cooker.
I eat nurungji snacks as a treat.
For the baby, I boiled the scorched rice until it was soft.

examples.ko: 식사 후에 누룽지를 한 그릇씩 줘요.
examples.en: They give each person a bowl of nurungji after the meal.

examples.ko: 누룽지 맛이 고소해서 자꾸 손이 가요.
examples.en: Nurungji tastes so nutty that I keep reaching for it.

explain: 밥솥 바닥에 눌어붙은 밥을 말해요. 거기에 물을 붓고 끓이면 '누룽지탕'이나 '숭늉'처럼 먹을 수 있고, 요즘은 과자나 차로도 팔아요. 맛은 '구수하다', '고소하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is the rice that sticks and browns on the bottom of the rice pot. If you add water and boil it, you can eat it as '누룽지탕' or as '숭늉', and these days it's also sold as snacks or tea. Its taste is described as '구수하다' or '고소하다'.

examples.en: The snowflakes stuck coldly to my face.
Big snowflakes are falling from the sky.
The child caught a snowflake on his tongue.
Every single snowflake has a different shape.
Snowflakes are fluttering down outside the window.
A snowflake lightly landed on my glove.

explain: '송이'는 꽃이나 포도, 눈처럼 덩어리로 모인 것을 세는 말이에요. 눈이 '내리다', '날리다'라고 하고, 크고 포슬포슬한 눈은 '함박눈'이라고 해요. 말할 때는 '눈'이라고만 해도 충분하고 눈송이는 하나하나를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: '송이' is a counter for things that come in clusters, like flowers, grapes and snow. Snow 'falls' (내리다) or 'drifts' (날리다), and big fluffy snow is '함박눈'. In speech '눈' alone is enough, and 눈송이 is used when talking about individual flakes.
